Defining the relationships for the Directed acyclic graph (DAG)

The structural relationships between health insurance coverage, blood sugar screening, and potential confounding pathways are represented in the Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) below.

Methods To ensure conditional exchangeability, peer-reviewed literature was assessed to identify known predictors of both health insurance coverage and preventative diabetes screening.

The DAG was first created using DAGGITY online and then modifed using the code below.

Potential Confounders Below are the the covariates included in the DAG:

  • Demographic / socioeconomic: age, sex, race/ethnicity, education, family income-to-poverty ratio, marital status, country of birth, interview language.
  • Health status / risk: BMI, self-rated general health, prior hypertension diagnosis.
  • Health behavior: ever-smoking.
nhanes_dag <- dagitty('dag {
"Blood Sugar Screening (Y)" [outcome,pos="1.058,1.374"]
"Country of birth" [pos="-1.175,-1.600"]
"Family income-to-poverty ratio" [pos="1.128,-1.885"]

Generating the DAG a format defined by the ggdag package

To create a readable DAG, the ggdag package uses a mixture of r-code and html.

In the proposed DAG, High blood pressure acts as a confounder for the causal pathway, while simultaneously serving as a collider for upstream variables such as Age, BMI, and Smoking status. While conditioning on a collider typically induces collider-stratification bias by opening backdoor paths between its parents, these newly opened paths are simultaneously blocked because the parent variables (i.e.Age, BMI, etc) are adjusted for within the model. For this reason, adjusting for High blood pressure would be considered statistically safe and would not introduce bias into our causal estimand.

dag_cleaned <- tidy_dagitty(nhanes_dag) %>%
  node_status() %>% 
  mutate(
    x     = x * 1.5,
    y     = y * 1.5,
    xend  = xend * 1.5,
    yend  = yend * 1.5,
    
  
    status = case_when(
      name == "Health-insurance coverage (A)" ~ "Exposure",
      name == "Blood Sugar Screening (Y)" ~ "Outcome",
      name %in% c("Acculturation") ~ "Unmeasured", 
      TRUE ~ "Adjusted" 
    )
  )

ggplot(dag_cleaned, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
  geom_dag_edges(
    arrow_directed = grid::arrow(length = unit(3, "mm"), type = "closed"),
    edge_colour = "black",
    edge_width = 0.5
  ) +

  geom_dag_node(aes(color = status), size = 12) +

  geom_dag_label_repel(
    aes(label = name),
    direction = "y",
    size = 2,
    box.padding = 0.1,
    point.padding = 0.1,
    segment.color = "grey75",
    segment.size = 0.5,
    label.size = 0.1,
    fill = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  theme_dag() +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Exposure"   = "#1f77b4", 
      "Outcome"    = "#d62728", 
      "Adjusted"   = "#2ca02c",
      "Unadjusted" = "#ff7f0e",
      "Unmeasured" = "#7f7f7f"
    ),
    name = "Variable Status"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) for 2017-2020 NHANES Data",
    subtitle = "Exposure: Insurance Status | Outcome: Blood Sugar Screening"
  ) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, color = "grey30"),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )
